name: Outline and Contour Generation
text:
# Outline and Contour Generation


## Overview
Outline and Contour Generation is a family of non-photorealistic volume rendering techniques that enhance perceptual clarity by explicitly rendering geometric boundaries as line primitives or stylized strokes [S2][S4, unofficial]. Unlike surface-based NPR, which relies on well-defined surfaces, this family operates on volumetric data by identifying regions of high gradient magnitude or specific curvature properties to estimate physical boundaries without predefined classification functions [S2, unofficial]. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [Line Illustration Detection](772-line-illustration-detection.md) by focusing on object silhouettes and feature contours rather than flow-aligned hatching, and from [LOG-based Silhouette Detection](6322-log-based-silhouette-detection.md) by utilizing various geometric and image-space heuristics for edge extraction rather than solely Laplacian-of-Gaussian responses.

## Shared principles
The family shares the fundamental goal of enhancing perceptual clarity through non-photorealistic edge representation. Common mechanisms include:
1.  **Edge Detection:** Identifying boundaries based on geometric properties (normals, curvature, topology) or image-space properties (depth, normal discontinuities) [S2][S3, S4, unofficial].
2.  **Line Rendering:** Converting detected edges into line primitives (strips, segments) or stylized strokes [S2][S3, S4, unofficial].
3.  **[Compositing](#2436-compositing.md):** Integrating these lines with the underlying volume or surface rendering, often using depth buffering for hidden line removal [S2][S3, S4, unofficial].

Volumetric illustration differs from surface-based NPR in several important ways [S2][S4, unofficial]. In surface NPR, surfaces (features) are well-defined, whereas with volumes, feature areas within the volume must be determined through analysis of local volumetric properties because volumetric features vary continuously throughout three-dimensional space [S2][S4, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Object Contour NPR](787-object-contour-npr.md)
[Object Contour NPR](#787-object-contour-npr.md) generates view-dependent line primitives that demarcate areas where an object's surface turns away from the viewer, effectively conveying shape through [boundary emphasis](#12217-boundary-emphasis.md). Unlike surface-based NPR, this method operates on volumetric data by identifying regions of high gradient magnitude, estimating physical boundaries without relying on predefined classification functions or voxel intensity values. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [Lasso Contour Rendering](#1855-lasso-contour-rendering.md) by utilizing a [geometry shader](#4369-geometry-shader-quads.md) to trace line-strips directly to the screen from selected particles, rather than recording strokes to a texture buffer.

### [Image Space Outline Generation](788-image-space-outline-generation.md)
[Image Space Outline Generation](#788-image-space-outline-generation.md) is a post-processing method that renders outlines by extracting edges from depth or normal maps. It solves the problem of defining perceptual boundaries in non-photorealistic rendering by leveraging the simplicity of screen-space buffers, distinguishing itself from analytical methods by operating directly on pixel data rather than geometric primitives.

### [Lasso Contour Rendering](1855-lasso-contour-rendering.md)
Lasso Contour Rendering is an interactive non-photorealistic volume rendering technique that allows users to manually define and visualize specific volumetric features using a free-form "lasso" selection tool. It solves the problem of isolating complex, continuous volumetric structures that lack sharp boundaries by enabling user-driven contour generation. It differs from its siblings, such as [Object Contour NPR](787-object-contour-npr.md) and [Curvature-Controlled Style Contours](5350-curvature-controlled-style-contours.md), by relying on explicit user [interaction](#41-interaction.md) to define the region of interest rather than automatic geometric or scalar-based detection.

### [Curvature-Controlled Style Contours](5350-curvature-controlled-style-contours.md)
[Curvature-Controlled Style Contours](#5350-curvature-controlled-style-contours.md) is a non-photorealistic volume rendering technique that generates outline contours with consistent visual thickness by regulating the detection threshold based on the normal curvature along the view direction. Unlike standard dot-product contours, which produce uncontrolled thickness variations (too thick on flat surfaces, too thin on fine structures), this method ensures that contours remain perceptually uniform across varying surface geometries. It builds on [Outline and Contour Generation](4137-outline-and-contour-generation.md) by integrating curvature-aware edge detection with [style transfer functions](#13031-style-transfer-and-illustrative-rendering.md) for color mapping.

### [Silhouette Rendering](7959-silhouette-rendering.md)
[Silhouette rendering](#7959-silhouette-rendering.md) is an object-space line rendering technique that extracts and stylizes significant edges (silhouettes and feature lines) from volumetric or surface data to enhance perceptual clarity and context. It distinguishes itself from image-space methods by processing geometry directly, allowing for precise hidden line removal and independent stroke stylization before compositing. It is particularly used to discriminate object classes based on specific features, such as highlighting lymph nodes touching critical structures in surgical planning.

### [Topological Landscape](8481-topological-landscape.md)
[Topological landscape](#8481-topological-landscape.md) is a visualization method that maps the topological structure of a scalar field's [contour tree](#9312-contour-tree.md) onto a 3D terrain model to enhance the perceptual clarity of volumetric features. It solves the problem of interpreting complex topological changes (merges and splits) in high-dimensional data by leveraging human intuition for reading terrain structures. It sets itself apart from [direct volume rendering](#1184-direct-volume-rendering.md) by abstracting the scalar field into a structural graph representation, and from other contour-based methods like [Outline and Contour Generation](4137-outline-and-contour-generation.md) by explicitly encoding topological events as geometric elevations rather than screen-space edges.

### [Boundary Enhancement Volume Style](10863-boundary-enhancement-volume-style.md)
[Boundary Enhancement Volume Style](#10863-boundary-enhancement-volume-style.md) is a non-photorealistic rendering technique designed to highlight feature bounds within volumetric data while simultaneously reducing visual noise. It addresses the challenge of distinguishing meaningful structures in continuous volumetric fields where feature areas are not well-defined as they are in surface-based rendering. Unlike sibling methods that focus on silhouette or contour lines, this style operates directly on volume boundaries to enhance perceptual clarity through edge emphasis.

### [Suggestive Contour Extraction](13101-suggestive-contour-extraction.md)
[Suggestive contour extraction](#13101-suggestive-contour-extraction.md) identifies surface locations where radial curvature is zero but increasing towards the viewer, complementing standard geometric contours to enhance shape perception. Unlike standard contours which mark the silhouette of the object relative to the camera, suggestive contours reveal the "hidden" curvature of the surface, particularly on convex regions, providing a more complete line drawing of the volume's form.

#### Ghosted Views with Contours
Ghosted Views with Contours is a technique where occluding context objects are reduced to contours to reveal pre-segmented internal structures [S1, unofficial]. The process involves:
1.  Pre-segmenting the most interesting internal structures (e.g., small internal organs) [S1, unofficial].
2.  Identifying context information (e.g., the body) that obscures the interesting structures [S1, unofficial].
3.  In areas of occlusion, reducing the visual representation of the context object to contours [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of using contours and outlines to enhance volumetric visualization has roots in illustrative visualization techniques applied to medical and scientific data. Early applications included cut-away visualizations for CT-angiography to visualize peripheral arteries, where bones and skin contours were rendered to provide spatial context [S1, unofficial]. The specific term "Ghosted Views with Contours" appears in the context of visualizing internal structures of a Leopard gecko, where the body was reduced to contours to reveal internal organs [S1, unofficial]. The broader family of Outline and Contour Generation methods has evolved to include object-space, image-space, and topology-based approaches to handle the continuous nature of volumetric data [S2][S4, unofficial].
